from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Music relies on a steady, consistent beat.",
            "This pulse acts like a clock for musicians.",
            "Think of a heartbeat keeping rhythm steady."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Prerequisite: The Metronome Pulse", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        bars = VGroup(*[Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE) for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(bars, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        timeline = Line(LEFT*2.5, RIGHT*2.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(timeline, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        pulse_dot = Dot(color="#00FFFF")
        pulse_dot.move_to(timeline.get_left())
        
        border = SurroundingRectangle(timeline, color="#FFD700", buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(bars))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        for bar in bars:
            self.play(bar.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=0.2)
            self.play(bar.animate.set_color(WHITE), run_time=0.2)
        
        self.play(Transform(bars, timeline))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.add(pulse_dot)
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(pulse_dot, timeline), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(Create(border))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Grouping the Beats: The Concept of the Bar", [
            "Music requires organization to stay together.",
            "We group beats into rhythmic measures.",
            "The downbeat signals a brand new cycle."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display three sets of four dots at #FFFFFF.
        dots = VGroup()
        for i in range(3):
            group = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
            self.place_at_grid(group, f"{chr(ord('B') + i*2)}{1}")
            dots.add(group)
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Group each set of four dots inside a rectangle at #FF00FF.
        rects = VGroup()
        for group in dots:
            rect = SurroundingRectangle(group, color="#FF00FF", buff=0.1)
            rects.add(rect)
        self.play(Create(rects))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the first dot of each group at #00FFFF.
        animations = []
        for group in dots:
            first_dot = group[0]
            animations.append(first_dot.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(*animations)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Time signatures look like math fractions.",
            "The top number counts beats per measure.",
            "The bottom number shows the note value.",
            "Four-four time means four quarter beats.",
            "The pie chart shows the measure's capacity."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Time Signature: The Mathematical Fraction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create Fraction 4/4
        fraction = MathTex(r"{4 \over 4}", font_size=120)
        top_digit = MathTex("4", font_size=120)
        bottom_digit = MathTex("4", font_size=120)
        
        top_digit.move_to(self.grid["B3"] + UP * 0.4)
        bottom_digit.move_to(self.grid["B3"] + DOWN * 0.4)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(fraction))
        self.place_at_grid(fraction, "B3")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.play(FadeOut(fraction))
        self.play(Write(top_digit))
        self.play(top_digit.animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Write(bottom_digit))
        self.play(bottom_digit.animate.set_color("#1E90FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        fraction_full = MathTex(r"{4 \over 4}", font_size=120)
        self.place_at_grid(fraction_full, "B3")
        self.play(FadeOut(top_digit), FadeOut(bottom_digit), Write(fraction_full))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        pie = VGroup(*[Sector(radius=1.5, angle=TAU/4, start_angle=i*TAU/4, color=c) for i, c in enumerate([BLUE, RED, GREEN, YELLOW])])
        self.place_at_grid(pie, "E3")
        self.play(Create(pie))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Applying the Theory: Rhythmic Patterns", [
            "Notes must fill the measure perfectly.",
            "Different durations add up to the total.",
            "Rhythm works like a musical puzzle."
        ])
        
        # Define notes
        notes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(8)])
        for i in range(8):
            self.place_at_grid(notes[i], f"{['B', 'D'][i//4]}{i%4 + 1}")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(notes), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        pattern_groups = VGroup(notes[0:4], notes[4:8])
        for group in pattern_groups:
            self.play(group.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(notes[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(notes[4].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Living Measure", [
            "Measures act as a shared grid.",
            "They allow everyone to play in sync.",
            "The whole band lands on one together."
        ])
        
        # Define elements
        metronome = Triangle(color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(metronome, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        notes = VGroup(*[MusicNote() for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT) # Placeholder
        self.place_at_grid(notes, 'D3', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Rotating(metronome, about_point=self.grid['B3'] + DOWN*0.5, radians=PI/4, run_time=1),
                  Rotating(metronome, about_point=self.grid['B3'] + DOWN*0.5, radians=-PI/2, run_time=1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(notes))
        self.play(notes.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(notes.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), 
                  metronome.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

class MusicNote(VMobject):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.add(Circle(radius=0.2), Line(UP*0.2, UP*0.8))
        self.set_fill(WHITE, opacity=1)

outline.topic: The Pulse of Rhythm: An Introduction to Music and Measure Theory
outline.target_audience: Middle school students or beginner music theory enthusiasts

sections.title: The Prerequisite: The Metronome Pulse
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a 'steady beat' as the fundamental unit of time. Explain that just as a heart beats, music relies on a consistent internal clock.
sections.example: A mechanical frog sitting on a log, blinking its eyes exactly once per second to represent a steady beat.

sections.title: Grouping the Beats: The Concept of the Bar
sections.content: Explain that music needs organization. We group beats into 'measures' (or bars) using a strong downbeat to signal the start of a new cycle.
sections.example: A row of 4 fireflies: the first one glows bright yellow (the '1' or downbeat), and the next three glow soft blue, creating a 4-beat cycle that repeats.

sections.title: The Time Signature: The Mathematical Fraction
sections.content: Translate musical notation into a visual fraction. The top number indicates how many beats per measure; the bottom number defines which note value receives one beat.
sections.example: A visual animation of a '4/4' fraction appearing above a musical staff, where a 'pie chart' is sliced into 4 equal segments to show the measure's capacity.

sections.title: Applying the Theory: Rhythmic Patterns
sections.content: Show how different note durations (whole, half, quarter) must add up exactly to the total value allowed by the time signature.
sections.example: A 'Music Tetris' game where the player must fit blocks (notes) into a frame (measure). If the measure is 4/4, a whole note block fills the entire space, while four quarter note blocks fill it perfectly.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Living Measure
sections.content: Summarize how measure theory acts as a grid that allows musicians to play together in perfect synchronization.
sections.example: An orchestra of different cartoon animals (a lion on drums, a bird on flute) all playing from the same '4/4' grid; even though they play different notes, they all land on the '1' together.
